posts.title: We built Optimus to profile our own Frappe work, then open-sourced it
posts.excerpt: System freezes under heavy load, lock wait timeouts, 'server is too busy' errors: we kept tracing them back to customization bottlenecks on client sites. So we built Optimus to find them, then open-sourced it for the Frappe ecosystem.
posts.author: Aerele Engineering

posts.title: Lens Code Audit: catch risky Frappe customizations before they ship
posts.excerpt: Most ERPNext upgrade pain starts in custom code. Lens reads your apps the way a senior reviewer would and flags the patterns that break - before they reach production.
posts.author: Aerele Engineering

posts.title: Lens Compatibility Check: know if your apps survive the next ERPNext upgrade
posts.excerpt: Upgrades stall on one question - will our customizations still work? Lens answers it up front with a per-app compatibility report against your target version.
posts.author: Aerele Engineering

posts.title: What 600+ merged PRs into Frappe taught us about upstream-first work
posts.excerpt: Forking is easy; contributing upstream is hard and worth it. The habits that got our patches merged into the framework your ERPNext runs on.
posts.author: Aerele Engineering

posts.title: Integrating ERPNext with India's banking rails: production lessons
posts.excerpt: NEFT, RTGS, UPI and host-to-host files in a regulated workflow. The retries, idempotency, and audit trails that kept it reliable when money was on the line.
posts.author: Aerele Engineering

posts.title: Why we built Lens - codifying migration audits into software
posts.excerpt: Years of migration reviews turned into a tool. What we automated, what still needs a senior human, and what we learned shipping our first product.
posts.author: Aerele Engineering
